column1: # reviewer-sources.tsv — the single reviewer-source registry (issue #1425).
# One row per third-party review bot (GitHub App) the org recognizes. This is the
# source of truth that three consumers agree with, so their lists can never drift:
#   * dev-lead's trust check   — scripts/dev-lead-intent.sh (TRUSTED_BOTS)
#   * the advisory approval gate — scripts/lib/advisory-review-gate.sh (ADVISORY_BOTS,
#                                  RATE_LIMIT_NOTICE_BOTS)
#   * the reviewer scorecard    — scripts/reviewer_report.sh (REVIEWER_BOTS)
# Read by scripts/lib/reviewer-sources.sh. Data, not code — register a reviewer by
# adding a row; tests/test_reviewer_sources.bats asserts the three consumer lists
# stay projections of this file and enforces the invariant below.
# THE #1425 INVARIANT — (can create a review thread) ⇒ (dev-lead may act on it):
#   any row with creates_threads=yes MUST have dev_lead_trusted=yes. A bot that
#   posts inline review comments creates a review thread, and an unresolved thread
#   trips required_review_thread_resolution and blocks the merge; if dev-lead is not
#   permitted to act on it, no automation can clear it (the 2026-08-02 deadlock,
#   root-caused to graphite-app). A source that only posts a top-level comment
#   (creates_threads=no) MAY be advisory-only-and-non-blocking (dev_lead_trusted=no)
#   with the reason recorded in the rationale column.
# schema_version: 3
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   login            — the bot's GraphQL App login (no "[bot]" suffix). dev-lead's
#                      webhook-facing trusted set appends "[bot]" to each login.
#   creates_threads  — yes|no: posts inline review comments (→ blocking review thread).
#   dev_lead_trusted — yes|no: in dev-lead's trusted set (dev-lead may act on it).
#   advisory_gate    — yes|no: one of the bots the advisory approval gate waits on.
#   check_run_name   — the exact check-run name this bot reports its review through,
#                      or "-" when it reports only via PR reviews/comments. A bot with
#                      a check_run_name posts each review as a check run (e.g. Graphite's
#                      "Graphite / AI Reviews"); a completed run whose summary says the
#                      review ran is a real response EVEN WITH ZERO comments and no PR
#                      review, so the scorecard fetches it separately (#1908). Data, not
#                      code: the scorecard reads this column instead of hard-coding logins.
#                      The advisory gate reads it too (#2005): a completed, conclusion=success
#                      run with this name on the PR's current head SHA counts as a clean
#                      submission from an advisory_gate=yes bot (failed/neutral/pending don't).
#   info_status_pattern — a case-sensitive regex (jq test()) matching a KNOWN CLEAN
#                      *informational* status comment from this bot that carries no
#                      finding and needs no disposition — e.g. SonarCloud's
#                      "Quality Gate passed". "-" when the bot posts no such comment.
#                      maintainer-comment-gate.sh (#1918) treats a comment authored by
#                      this login whose body matches this pattern as ADDRESSED, so a
#                      clean status re-posted on every push never deadlocks approval.
#                      It must NOT match the bot's finding-bearing comments (SonarCloud's
#                      "Quality Gate failed" must still block) — the gate fails closed on
#                      anything this pattern does not match. Data, not hard-coded logins.
#                      FOR NO-FINDING SERVICE NOTICES ONLY (#1995): declare one only for a
#                      usage-limit / trial-ended / "review limit reached" / clean-status
#                      message that carries no finding. Anchor it tightly — several required
#                      literals in sequence, like the sonarqubecloud row — so it cannot match
#                      a review body that merely mentions a limit. Match the bot's COMPLETE
#                      known notice body, anchored at both ends (^ … \s*$), so a notice
#                      followed by finding text never clears; allow leading HTML marker
#                      comments with ^\s*(<!--[^>]*-->\s*)* when the bot prefixes one.
#                      Never reach for this column to wave away an inconvenient review: a
#                      finding-producing reviewer (codeant-ai, graphite-app) carries "-" and
#                      its findings go through dev-lead's verified-fix flow.
#   rationale        — why this bot is classified as it is.
# login

column1: chatgpt-codex-connector
column6: ^(You have reached your Codex usage limits?( for code reviews)?\.(\s+You can see your limits in the (\[Codex usage dashboard\]\([^)\s]*\)|Codex usage dashboard)\.)?(\s+To continue using code reviews, you can upgrade your account or add credits to your account and enable them for code reviews in your \[settings\]\([^)\s]*\)\.)?|To use Codex here, (\[create an environment for this repo\]\([^)\s]*\)|create an environment for this repo)\.)\s*$
column7: Inline review comments (pull_request_review_comment); dev-lead addresses the findings. Its out-of-quota "You have reached your Codex usage limit[s for code reviews …]" notice — short and long forms alike — carries no finding, so the gate auto-clears it (#1995, #1993). Its "To use Codex here, create an environment for this repo." notice carries no finding either and clears the same way (#2255). Anchored to the body start and to the end of the notice sentence, so neither a comment that merely quotes the notice nor one that opens with its words and goes on to a finding can clear; a real review body does not match and still blocks. Dropped from the approval-wait set (advisory_gate=no, #1997) because zero reviews were observed across eight consecutive PRs (#1888, #1887, #1873, #1799, #1796, #1794, #1793, #1770), measured 2026-09-23. Stays dev-lead-trusted and on the #1220 scorecard; it leaves only the approval-wait set.

column1: coderabbitai
column6: ^\s*(<!--[^>]*-->\s*)*Review limit reached — you have used up your prepaid credits\.?\s*$
column7: Inline review comments; tracked by the scorecard and rate-limit detector but not part of the advisory approval-wait set. The pattern matches only a STANDALONE "Review limit reached — you have used up your prepaid credits" notice, a documented form that has NOT been observed live (#1995). The notice CodeRabbit actually posts is the OSS "Review limit reached / You've used all free OSS reviews…" block, embedded in its full summary comment beside the separately throttled Security Architecture Review. That summary can carry real findings while the code review is rate-limited (PR #2000), so the pattern deliberately does NOT match the OSS notice: matching it would clear the whole summary, findings included (#2008; the #1995 "do not widen" rule). The summary is dispositioned per section through dev-lead's flow instead, and no CodeRabbit comment carrying a finding-bearing section (reviewer_sources_finding_section_pattern) can be auto-cleared. A real review body does not match and still blocks.

column1: sonarqubecloud
column6: \*\*Quality Gate passed\*\*[\s\S]*\[0 New issues\][\s\S]*\[0 Security Hotspots\]
column7: Top-level quality-gate comment only — no inline review threads; trusted so dev-lead acts on the comment via the issue-comment path. Its "Quality Gate passed" status is re-posted on every push and carries no finding, so the gate auto-clears it (#1918); "Quality Gate failed" does not match and still blocks.

column1: graphite-app
column7: Inline review comments AND clean passes reported ONLY as the "Graphite / AI Reviews" check run (no PR review) — the scorecard must read that check run or every clean pass is miscounted as No response (#1908). Root cause of the 2026-08-02 unclearable-thread deadlock — trusted so dev-lead can act on its findings (#1425). Kept at advisory_gate=yes under #1997: its zero-review count is a measurement artefact (a clean pass posts only the check run, invisible to the reviews API), not an absence of signal; its 2026-08-21 silence was a lapsed 30-day trial and the org moved to the paid plan on 2026-09-22, so do NOT re-drop it. The advisory gate counts a successful check run at the current head as graphite's clean submission (#2005), so a clean PR reaches quorum without waiting out the head-age timeout.
